title: Making UI is the hardest part, anyone else?
author: Kashmakers
selftext:
I don't mean designing it. I'm a graphic designer, so I can design my own UI and create all the elements for it. But instructing the AI to connect to my visuals and handle navigation, as well as execute the commands for that particular button etc. is the hardest part of using vibecoding with game dev.

I had a simple title screen with 3 options; new game, continue, exit game. Simple you'd think, but my god, for some reason the mouse would continuously not detect it was hovering the correct option. It'll take me days/weeks to go through all the bugs and errors. When the AI has to connect to something visual and handle navigation is where it tends to break.

Or maybe it's just a Godot thing. Probably a Godot thing.

comments.author: xFkinD
comments.body:
Are you using images as reference for the AI to generate your UI? 
I personally don't know much about UI/UX but I tend to take a long time improving that part or remaking the UI of my projects.

replies.author: Kashmakers
replies.body: It's not generating my UI, I've already got it set up in Godot. It just needs code to connect to it and make it work properly. So I'm explaining in a very long prompt what every node does, what it should do, how to navigate to it, how active/inactive buttons look like or should switch textures to etc.

replies.author: Kashmakers
replies.body: I am working with Cursor. Sonnet/Opus to plan, usually Auto (Composer) to build.

comments.author: xFkinD
comments.body:
Also, when using a game engine together with AI I suggest you actually learn a bit about the engine.
From my experience, AI isnt very good at the low code part of game engines, such as node conection and so on.

replies.author: Kashmakers
replies.body: It really isn't good at node connection indeed. I understand the node system in Godot quite well at this point, I can make really fancy UI. I just know zero about coding, which I let the AI handle.

replies.author: magicpenguin94
replies.body:
The problem with this approach is that you'd have no idea if the code is actually doing what you instructed it to do as the ai love to make its own assumptions and decisions. 

I can try and see if I can help you understand how to work with the ai to get better code if you want to DM me.

comments.author: mrpoopybruh
comments.body: UI takes forever, I hate it.

comments.author: Microtom_
comments.body: Nano banana is pretty good at it.

comments.author: Bethk_Parrish
comments.body: Honestly sounds like normal UI pain to me. Hover states and input detection can get weird fast, even without AI in the mix.

replies.author: Kashmakers
replies.body:
It's been a pain for sure, sometimes it won't detect my mouse, or that it's left the area, or that a child within the button itself still needs to count as the whole button.

That, and I have to keep testing it with controller input, which means I need to introduce a navigation delay as well (otherwise controller goes brrr).

comments.author: PenniesInTheNameOf
comments.body: Anyone have unlimited AI? A lot of games could be coded as a single script if the AI wasn’t so limited. Like I can only get 10,800 or so characters fed into my pro chatgpt. I have single scripts running 25,000 plus. Spent the last few weeks modularizing (pulling functions out and reconnecting) to reduce my character count to accelerate debugging. Migration is dropping functionality ALL over the place along with UI failing to migrate for different devices… spending a week on turning a functioning system into trash is disheartening.

replies.author: Kashmakers
replies.body: I think you need to switch AI. Try Claude Code or Cursor; it has access to your entire database and can make agentic changes to the files, there's no file limit. I wouldn't bother uploading one script at a time to ChatGPT.

comments.author: MakanLagiDud3
comments.body: As someone who does web dev, yes it is.

comments.author: Financial_Land_5429
comments.body: Antigravity is quite good with phaser 3, even with the UI

comments.author: MakkoMakkerton
comments.body:
I've used majority of GLM 5 for coding and have no interaction issues, but AI generally is not a master of uo/ux, tis why 90%of vibecoded projects look the same.

For UI what I do is ask the LLM what it thinks would be good to add imagery wise, I then take the ideas and make images either with veo/gpt. Things like health bars and borders and loading screens/title screens I've found take the most time because AI can build the game, but struggles to make it look "pretty"

comments.author: HealthyWest6482
comments.body: valid. codex will tell me he's ready to budget (???) and index enemy action spend across 15 different docs and pull runtime data to meticulously balance 83 categories but wont ever one pass "add a start button... and make it clickable".

comments.author: qwertyasdfghzxcvbnui
comments.body:
Same thing for me in Godot with the hover text. And it cropped up again when adding full controller support 😅

For other UI elements, instead of asking the ai to arrange it try "I need these elements to be scalable and have adjustable padding for text as well as being able to move them around on the page. Please let me know the exact lines for each structure for XYZ window"

Then just assist manually. That's been my quickest workflow 😁

replies.author: Kashmakers
replies.body:
> Same thing for me in Godot with the hover text. And it cropped up again when adding full controller support

Thiiiiis. I need to keep testing keyboard, mouse *and* controller. It's mouse and controller that always seem to misfire. With controller I need to add a navigation delay otherwise it just goes brrr. With mouse, sometimes Godot doesn't understand that the children of a node *counts* as still being in the same button.

comments.author: DatabaseConstant7870
comments.body: Okay so I use cursor with unity, I literally told it “do research on tony hawk games, focus on the ui that tells you what trick you do and points you get, recreate UI that is in the same style for my game, I’m giving you consent to download free assets and import them in the project, please get this done correctly with no errors” and it did it. Cursor may be the fix to everyone’s UI problems

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: Also cursor only went for assets that were free for commercial use without me telling it to.

replies.author: Kashmakers
replies.body:
I am using cursor, actually. My prompt for a menu was much longer with specific details, as I know how I want it to look and work.

But it was mostly struggling against Godot itself, there's a lot of native navigation in Godot that was working against me.

> with no errors

That's not how it works 😂

comments.author: Old-Persimmon-466
comments.body: From my experience, the best approach is to prototype the UI layer by layer, usually starting with Gemini for quick drafts, then refining each part as I go. That’s how I built my web game, and it really helped me stay organized and spot issues early. If you’re curious, you can check out what I made at [https://artpiece.app](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/tomru/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/0870c2a0c7/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html).
